open_questions: Depth is not stable (sectors.p_constant 1.085e-11, per-sector 10068 ppm sector 11, 4304 ppm sector 37, 3083 ppm sector 64 ppm, transit p_consistent 0.00152); star is spotted (teff 3256 K K/M dwarf, phase_curve amplitude 6040 ppm ratio_to_depth 1.315, variability_chi2_dof 17.28, TIC-STAR radius 0.333 vs Gaia FLAME 0.395 and GSP-Phot 0.401); need RV to confirm mass and Gaia epoch photometry/light-curve detrending to test spot contamination vs dilution, despite centroid on_target (neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0).
dossier.public_summary: A 2.5 Earth-radius dip repeats every 1.03 days on the target M dwarf with a flat bottom and no odd-even or secondary eclipse. Centroid imaging rules out a background eclipsing binary as the cause, leaving a small-planet transit as the best explanation, even though the depth appears to change between sectors and seasons.

reasons.why: difference imaging in sector 11 places the dip on the target and rules out the neighbours that could otherwise cause it; closest suspect 25.7 arcsec away is 9 sigma from centroid.
flat-bottomed shape favours a transiting planet over a grazing/stellar eclipse.
no odd/even depth difference versus EB at twice period.
no secondary eclipse detected (snr well below 5 and below best_brightening_snr 9.822).

planet-sized for a 0.333 Rsun M dwarf; consistent with stellar density even with long duration (1.494 h observed vs 0.8991 h central, ratio 1.66) indicating eccentric/impact-angle variation, not a star.
